Run every scenario of a project version in new R sessions

Source: R/run_scenarios.R
run_scenarios.Rd

run_scenarios() runs <home>/<version>_run.R once for each simulation of each scenario, each time in a new R session. It then stacks the simulations of each scenario and checks the assertions of the project.

Usage

run_scenarios(
  version,
  scenario = NULL,
  home = ".",
  workers = 1,
  resume = FALSE
)

Arguments

version

The version, for example "v01".

scenario

NULL for every scenario, or a character vector of the scenarios to run.

home

The project folder.

workers

The number of simulations that run at the same time, one whole number of 1 or more. Each simulation runs in its own new R session.

resume

FALSE runs every simulation of the chosen scenarios. TRUE keeps each simulation with results from the same code, and runs the others. See the section Resume.

Value

Invisibly, a data.frame of every assertion, with the columns scenario, assertion, expected, observed and pass.

Details

run_scenarios() does these steps in this order:

  1. It reads CFG$scenarios in a new R session that sources <version>_functions/ with org::initialize_project(). The R session of the caller does not change. It stops when a scenario other than "real" has no function expect_<scenario>(). It checks every chosen scenario before it runs any of them.

  2. With resume = TRUE, it chooses the simulations to keep, and prints one line for each of them.

  3. It deletes these files, and it stops before any run when one of them stays:

    • the check.csv of each chosen scenario.

    • the stacked results.qs2 of each chosen scenario with more than 1 simulation.

    • the results.qs2 and the run.ok of each simulation that it runs.

    Files of the scenarios that it does not run stay as they are.

  4. It runs the script once for each simulation that it does not keep. Each run is a new R session with the arguments scenario=<name> sim=<k>, and with home as the working directory. At most workers runs go at the same time. The stdout and the stderr of each run go to run.log in the results folder of the simulation. Each run writes run.log again, also a run that succeeds.

    A run succeeds when all of these hold:

    • It quits with status 0, so end_if_fake_scenario() can end the run of a fake scenario.

    • Its results.qs2 exists and passes check_results().

    • manifest$scenario, manifest$sim and manifest$sims are those of the simulation.

    After a run that succeeds, run_scenarios() writes run.ok beside run.log. run.ok holds one line, the md5 of results.qs2. A run that stops after it writes results.qs2 thus has no run.ok. This is also the case when the caller is interrupted. run.log and run.ok are run artefacts. List both in the .gitignore of the project.

    Each other run fails. For a run that fails, run_scenarios() prints the whole run.log with cat(). After the first failure, it starts no new run, and the runs that started go on to their end. It then stops with an error that names the scenario, the simulation and the run.log of each failed run. It stacks and checks no scenario.

  5. For each scenario with more than 1 simulation, it stacks the files <version>_results/<scenario>/sim_<kkkk>/results.qs2 into <version>_results/<scenario>/results.qs2. It stops when the files are not exactly the simulations 1 to sims. After sims in CFG$scenarios becomes smaller, the folders of the higher simulations stay. Stacking then stops, and the error names their files. Delete those folders to stack again. The section Stacking gives the rules.

  6. For each scenario that has a function expect_<scenario>() in <version>_functions/, it calls that function on the results of the scenario in a new R session. expect_real() is optional. The function MUST return a data.frame with at least one row and the columns assertion, expected, observed and pass. run_scenarios() writes it to <version>_results/<scenario>/check.csv and prints it.

Each of these counts as one failed assertion, and run_scenarios() writes it to check.csv too:

  • expect_<scenario>() stops with an error. The assertion holds the error message.

  • expect_<scenario>() returns zero rows.

  • expect_<scenario>() returns something other than a data.frame with the four columns.

After every scenario is done, run_scenarios() stops when a value of pass is not TRUE. The error lists the failed assertions.

Stacking

The stacked results hold every element of the results of simulation 1, in the same order. These rules apply at each depth:

  • A data.frame gets a first column sim, and the rows of the simulations in order. It keeps the class of simulation 1, so a data.table stays a data.table.

  • A list is stacked element by element, and pbn matches the elements by name. So each element of a list MUST have its own name. An unnamed or partly named list stops stacking. A scenario with 1 simulation MAY hold such a list.

  • Each other element becomes a list with one entry for each simulation, named sim_0001, sim_0002 and so on. This includes an atomic vector, a matrix, a factor, a date and NULL.

Stacking stops when two simulations differ in the structure at one path. The error names the path and the two simulations. Examples:

  • a list with other names or another length.

  • a data.frame with other columns, a column of another class, or a factor column with other levels.

  • a list in the place of a data.frame, or NULL in the place of a value.

Stacking also stops on a data.frame with a column sim, because pbn adds that column.

The manifest is that of simulation 1. In it, sim and n_rows_data are NA, sims is the number of simulations, and stacked is TRUE. For a fake scenario, stacking stops when a simulation has no valid manifest$fake_md5, or when the simulations do not have one value of it. It also stops when the simulations do not have one value of manifest$settings.

A scenario with 1 simulation is not stacked. Its results.qs2 is the file that the run wrote.

Workers

Each simulation depends only on its scenario and its number, so workers does not change the results files or check.csv. Only the order of the lines on the console can change. pbn does not limit the threads that R or the BLAS library starts in each R session.

Resume

With resume = TRUE, run_scenarios() keeps a simulation when all of these hold:

  • Its results.qs2 exists and passes check_results().

  • Its run.ok exists and holds the md5 of results.qs2 now. So the run completed, and nothing changed results.qs2 after it.

  • manifest$scenario, manifest$sim and manifest$sims are those of the simulation.

  • manifest$source_md5 is the md5 of the files of <version>_run.R and <version>_functions/ now.

  • For a fake scenario, manifest$fake_md5 is the md5 of the code of fake_<scenario>() now.

Each other simulation runs again, and the console line of its start gives the reason. The stacking and the expect_ assertions always run again.

Resume does not find a change in the real data, or in the version of R or of a package. It also does not find a change in a file outside <version>_run.R and <version>_functions/. After such a change, use resume = FALSE.

See also

Other project setup: end_if_fake_scenario(), initialize_project(), use_scenario()

Examples

# \donttest{
home <- file.path(tempdir(), "pbn_run_scenarios_example")
dir.create(file.path(home, "v01_functions"), recursive = TRUE)
dir.create(file.path(home, "data"))
utils::write.csv(data.frame(x = 1:4), file.path(home, "data", "d.csv"))
writeLines(
  c(
    "CFG <- list(",
    "  scenarios = data.frame(scenario = c('real', 'null'), sims = c(1, 2))",
    ")",
    "fake_null <- function(dir) {",
    "  utils::write.csv(data.frame(x = rnorm(4)), file.path(dir, 'd.csv'))",
    "}",
    "expect_null <- function(results) {",
    "  n <- length(unique(results$estimates$sim))",
    "  data.frame(assertion = 'two simulations', expected = 2,",
    "    observed = n, pass = n == 2)",
    "}"
  ),
  file.path(home, "v01_functions", "_cfg.R")
)
writeLines(
  c(
    'p <- pbn::initialize_project("v01", home = ".", data_raw = "data")',
    "d <- utils::read.csv(file.path(p$data_raw, 'd.csv'))",
    "pbn::save_results(",
    "  estimates = data.frame(term = 'mean_x', estimate = mean(d$x)),",
    "  n_rows = nrow(d),",
    "  d = d",
    ")"
  ),
  file.path(home, "v01_run.R")
)
pbn::run_scenarios("v01", home = home)
#> pbn: scenario real, simulation 1: started
#> pbn: scenario real, simulation 1: ran
#> pbn: scenario null, simulation 1: started
#> pbn: scenario null, simulation 1: ran
#> pbn: scenario null, simulation 2: started
#> pbn: scenario null, simulation 2: ran
#> Assertions of the scenario "null":
#>        assertion expected observed pass
#>  two simulations        2        2 TRUE
stacked <- pbn::read_results("v01", scenario = "null", home = home)
stacked$estimates
#>   sim   term    estimate
#> 1   1 mean_x  0.07921043
#> 2   2 mean_x -0.06364893
stacked$n_rows
#> $sim_0001
#> [1] 4
#> 
#> $sim_0002
#> [1] 4
#> 

unlink(home, recursive = TRUE)
# }
